issue_paraphrase: When a struct that is given an internal tag (the tag attribute) has a field marked flattened whose type is itself an internally or adjacently tagged enum, serializing the struct emits the wrong tag string at the point where the flattened enum's content appears: the value that should carry the enum's own tag/name is written out with the outer struct's tag/name instead. Deserialization reads the same tokens back correctly, so data serialized by this combination does not round-trip as expected and any consumer that checks the enum tag fails or misparses the output.
fix_summary: Extracted the serialization of the internally tagged struct's own tag field into a separate helper emitted before the flatten/field serialization, and computes the map length hint from whether that tag field exists instead of inserting the tag emit at position 0 of the shared field list. With the old insert(0), the flattened enum's own serialization (which uses the visitor-inlined field list) picked up the outer struct's tag binding.

issue_paraphrase: Deserializing an adjacently tagged enum - an enum that is represented as a map containing one key for the variant tag and one key for the content - fails whenever the map also holds any other, unrelated keys. The deserializer treats the first key that is neither the tag nor the content as a hard error, so maps produced by other sources that carry extra metadata fields cannot be parsed at all, even though unknown fields are silently ignored everywhere else in the library. When the strict deny-unknown-fields option is set, those extra keys should instead be rejected deliberately, and when it is not set they should be skipped transparently.
fix_summary: Added a TagContentOtherField visitor that classifies each map key as tag, content or other; generated deserialization code for adjacently tagged enums now loops, skipping and consuming 'other' keys (values read via IgnoredAny) until the tag/content keys are found, when deny_unknown_fields is unset. When deny_unknown_fields is set it keeps using the strict visitor that errors on any other key, so the option is now actually honored instead of being the universal behavior.
